evidence_gaps_add: No linked comparison covers tumour-only calling, FFPE tissue, ctDNA or targeted panels.
No peer-reviewed HG008 small-variant caller comparison was found; the GIAB HG008 somatic small-variant benchmark is a draft.

SEQC2 HCC1395 whole-genome caller comparisons (Xiao et al. 2021; NeuSomatic 2022 Additional file 2) were not extracted: the first is not open access through Europe PMC and the second prints its tables only in a PDF with rotated headers.

Guille et al. 2025 Tables S1-S2 (four development datasets, including PERMED-01 clinical breast cancer exomes, under four post-alignment procedures) and Wang et al. 2020 Tables S3-S8 (deep targeted and exome dilution series) are not transcribed in this bounded intake.
No linked study reports interval estimates for per-caller precision, recall or F1.
Caller versions differ between studies (for example MuTect2 from GATK v3.7-0 in Wang et al. 2020 and Mutect2 4.2.2.0 in Guille et al. 2025); no study evaluates current releases of every caller.
evidence_gaps_keep: Individual-condition confidence intervals are unreported in the source tables.
Exact caller release versions are not extracted from the primary article.
No foundation-model component is evaluated in this bounded intake.
use_case_changes.evidence_gaps_note: The first two kept gaps describe the Lancet paper only; the integrator may prefix them with 'Lancet paper:'. DeepSomatic, NeuSomatic and VarNet are supervised deep-learning callers, not foundation models, so the third gap still holds.
exclusions_proposed: FFPE samples, targeted panels, ctDNA, tumour-only calling, copy-number and structural variation

Callers other than Lancet/Strelka2 not transcribed in this bounded intake (Strelka, MuTect, MuTect2, LoFreq rows exist in the source but are not all ingested; LoFreq/MuTect2 unselected rows are internally inconsistent in the source and are excluded)
use_case_changes.exclusions_note: The first current exclusion lists 'Real clinical tumour specimens'. Wang et al. 2020 adds real tumour WGS (CLL, AML, MB) scored against curated research truth sets, so the proposal drops that phrase and keeps clinical validation out of scope through clinical_scope. The second exclusion is unchanged.
use_case_changes.setting_proposed: Published tumour-normal comparisons: a real-read virtual-tumour spike-in (Lancet paper, 80x/40x WGS), four simulated DREAM WGS pairs and four real tumour or cell-line WGS pairs with curated truth sets (Wang et al. 2020), and a held-out SEQC2 HCC1395 exome sample (Guille et al. 2025), each measuring per-caller SNV and indel precision, recall and F1.
use_case_changes.decision_proposed: Inspect the per-dataset precision, recall and F1 of the callers and ensembles in the linked comparisons, matched to the intended sequencing type, coverage and normal-sample regime, before selecting a caller and designing a validation protocol.
use_case_changes.pin_warning: Changing exclusions, setting or decision alters fields pinned by the reviewed judgement use-case-mapping-amp-20261007-issue10-lancet-virtual-tumor, which would then be withheld until it is re-reviewed and re-pinned (npm run use-cases:repin). Adding assessed_by links, evidence gaps, source_ids and citation locators does not withhold it.

summary_proposal.value: Three comparisons are linked, and their values cannot be pooled: truth sets, sequencing and caller versions differ. Values below are rounded to two decimals. On a held-out SEQC2 HCC1395 exome sample, an academic group that did not develop the callers (Guille et al. 2025) found that DeepSomatic had the highest F1 of 16 single callers for SNVs (0.90) and of 13 for indels (0.81). Mutect and Mutect2 reached 0.85 and 0.83 for SNVs; Strelka reached 0.64, with precision 0.51. The authors' own voting ensembles reached 0.88 and 0.88 for SNVs and 0.75 and 0.74 for indels. The indel truth set has 50 variants, the model type of the DeepSomatic run is unclear, and the NeuSomatic model used was trained on the same cell line. On eight whole-genome tumour-normal pairs (Wang et al. 2020, caller versions from that study), a majority vote of four or seven callers had the highest SNV F1 on seven of the eight pairs. The best non-ensemble configuration reached SNV F1 0.92 to 0.96 on simulated DREAM sets 1 to 3, but 0.70 to 0.81 on three real tumours, where most callers had precision below 0.6 against curated truth sets that may be incomplete. Indel F1 on the real tumours and the COLO829 cell line was at most 0.72 for every configuration. In the Lancet developers' own virtual-tumour test, Lancet and Strelka2 both reached SNV F1 0.85, with indel F1 0.81 and 0.77. None of the linked studies covers FFPE tissue, ctDNA, tumour-only calling or targeted panels.

concerns_for_reviewer.locator: Results 'Validation' paragraph 2 versus Supplementary Table S7 H17, H32
concerns_for_reviewer.message: The prose says the retained ensembles surpass 'the best individual tool' by 2.7% (SNV F1 0.880) and 10.2% (indel F1 0.752), but Table S7 prints higher single-caller F1 for DeepSomatic-WES (SNV 0.9006, indel 0.8119). The stated gains match Mutect (0.853) and Mutect2 (0.650), so the prose appears to compare against classic callers only. Table values are recorded.
